debutant.question: What event marks the beginning of the Bible?
debutant.explanation: The Bible begins with the story of God's creation of the world in 6 days (Genesis 1).

debutant.question: In what chronological order did these events occur?
debutant.explanation: The order is: Abraham (c. 2000 BC) → Moses (c. 1300 BC) → David (c. 1000 BC) → Jesus (c. 1 BC).

debutant.question: How many days did it take God to create the world?
debutant.explanation: God created in 6 days and rested on the 7th day (Genesis 1-2).

debutant.question: How many years did the Israelites wander in the desert?
debutant.explanation: The Israelites wandered for 40 years in the wilderness because of their lack of faith (Numbers 14:33).

debutant.question: What was the first event following the creation of man?
options: The fall of Adam and Eve
debutant.explanation: After the creation of Adam and Eve, the Bible recounts their sin and fall in the Garden of Eden (Genesis 3).

debutant.question: Before or after the flood was the Tower of Babel located?
options: The Tower of Babel and the Flood are simultaneous
debutant.explanation: The Tower of Babel was built after the flood by Noah's descendants (Genesis 11:1-9).

debutant.question: Which king reigned before David in Israel?
debutant.explanation: Saul was the first king of Israel, anointed by the prophet Samuel before David succeeded him (1 Samuel 9-11).

debutant.question: Who reigned after David?
debutant.explanation: Solomon, son of David, succeeded him on the throne of Israel (1 Kings 1-2).

debutant.question: What event followed the death of Solomon?
options: The division of the kingdom in two
debutant.explanation: After Solomon's death, the kingdom was divided into two: Israel in the north and Judah in the south (1 Kings 12).

debutant.question: Which people destroyed Jerusalem and took the Jews into exile?
debutant.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar and the Babylonians destroyed Jerusalem and the Temple in 586 BC. (2 Kings 25).

debutant.question: Who allowed the Jews to return to Israel after the Babylonian exile?
debutant.explanation: Cyrus the Great of Persia issued an edict in 538 BC. allowing Jews to return to Israel (Ezra 1:1-4).

debutant.question: In what period of history was the birth of Jesus located?
options: Under the reign of Herod the Great and the Roman Empire
During the reign of Alexander the Great
debutant.explanation: Jesus was born during the reign of Herod the Great, when Judea was under Roman rule (Matthew 2:1).

debutant.question: What event marks the beginning of the Christian Church?
debutant.explanation: Pentecost, 50 days after Easter, marks the birth of the Church with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit (Acts 2).

debutant.question: In what order did these events of the Passion occur?
debutant.explanation: Order: The Last Supper (Thursday evening) → Gethsemane and arrest → trial → Crucifixion (Friday) → Resurrection (Sunday morning).

debutant.question: How many days did Jesus appear after his resurrection before his ascension?
debutant.explanation: Jesus manifested himself for 40 days after his resurrection before ascending to heaven (Acts 1:3).

debutant.question: Quel prophète a vécu avant Moïse : Abraham ou Élie ?
options: Les deux ont vécu après Moïse
debutant.explanation: Abraham vécut environ 700 ans avant Moïse, tandis qu'Élie vécut environ 400 ans après Moïse (IXe siècle av. J.-C.).

debutant.question: Qui a été créé en premier selon la Genèse : Adam ou Ève ?
options: Ils ont été créés simultanément le 3e jour
debutant.explanation: Selon Genèse 2:7-22, Dieu forma d'abord Adam de la poussière, puis créa Ève à partir d'une de ses côtes.

debutant.question: Quel événement a eu lieu juste après la sortie d'Égypte ?
options: La construction du Temple de Salomon
La traversée de la Mer Rouge
debutant.explanation: Peu après avoir quitté l'Égypte, les Israélites traversèrent la Mer Rouge à pied sec (Exode 14).

debutant.question: Combien de jours a duré la pluie du déluge au temps de Noé ?
debutant.explanation: It rained on the earth for 40 days and 40 nights (Genesis 7:12).

debutant.question: What biblical book recounts the events immediately following the death of Moses?
debutant.explanation: The book of Joshua begins just after Moses' death with the entry into the Promised Land (Joshua 1:1-2).

debutant.question: In what order did these three characters live?
debutant.explanation: Abraham is the father of Isaac, who is himself the father of Jacob (Genesis 21 and 25).

debutant.question: What event comes before the reign of kings in Israel?
options: The ministry of John the Baptist
debutant.explanation: After Joshua, Israel was ruled by Judges for several centuries before the establishment of the monarchy under Saul (1 Samuel 8).

debutant.question: How many years did David reign over Israel in total?
debutant.explanation: David reigned for 40 years: 7 and a half years in Hebron over Judah, then 33 years in Jerusalem over all Israel (2 Samuel 5:4-5).

debutant.question: How many years did Solomon reign over Israel?
debutant.explanation: Like David, Solomon reigned for 40 years in Jerusalem over all Israel (1 Kings 11:42).

debutant.question: Which prophet anointed Saul and then David as kings of Israel?
debutant.explanation: The prophet Samuel received the order from God to anoint Saul (1 Samuel 10) and then David (1 Samuel 16).

debutant.question: Which event happened first: the birth of Moses or the birth of Joseph?
options: They took place the same year
That of Joshua before the two
debutant.explanation: Joseph lived long before Moses: it was under Joseph that Jacob's family settled in Egypt (Genesis 46; Exodus 1).

debutant.question: How many years old was Joseph when he was sold by his brothers?
debutant.explanation: Genesis 37:2 indicates that Joseph was 17 years old when he shepherded the flock with his brothers.

debutant.question: At what age did Joseph become governor of Egypt before Pharaoh?
debutant.explanation: Joseph was 30 years old when he appeared before Pharaoh to interpret his dreams (Genesis 41:46).

debutant.question: How old was Moses when he died on Mount Nebo?
debutant.explanation: Moses was 120 years old when he died, and his eyesight was not impaired (Deuteronomy 34:7).

debutant.question: How many days did Jesus fast in the desert before being tempted?
debutant.explanation: Jesus fasted 40 days and 40 nights in the desert after his baptism (Matthew 4:2).

debutant.question: At what age did Jesus begin his public ministry according to Luke?
debutant.explanation: Luke 3:23 states that Jesus was about 30 years old when he began his ministry.

debutant.question: What event immediately preceded Jesus' public ministry?
options: His baptism by John the Baptist
debutant.explanation: Jesus was baptized by John the Baptist in the Jordan River early in his ministry (Matthew 3:13-17).

debutant.question: How many days after Jesus' birth was his circumcision?
debutant.explanation: According to the Law of Moses, Jesus was circumcised on the 8th day and given his name (Luke 2:21).

debutant.question: At what age was Jesus found in the Temple discussing with the doctors of the Law?
debutant.explanation: At the age of 12, Jesus stayed in Jerusalem during the Passover festival to listen to and question the teachers (Luke 2:42-46).

debutant.question: Which king ruled Judea during the massacre of the innocents in Bethlehem?
debutant.explanation: Herod the Great ordered the massacre of children under two years old in Bethlehem after the visit of the wise men (Matthew 2:16).

debutant.question: In what order did these events in the life of Jesus take place?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem, baptized around 30 years old, crucified in Jerusalem, resurrected on the 3rd day and ascended to heaven 40 days later.

debutant.question: How much time passed between Jesus' death and his resurrection?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was crucified on Friday and resurrected on the third day, Sunday morning (Luke 24:1-7).

debutant.question: How many days separate Easter from Pentecost in the biblical tradition?
debutant.explanation: Pentecost means 'fiftieth': it occurs 50 days after the feast of Easter (Leviticus 23:16; Acts 2:1).

debutant.question: Who was stoned first as a Christian martyr in the Acts of the Apostles?
debutant.explanation: Stephen, one of the seven deacons, was stoned to death before Saul of Tarsus (Acts 7:54-60).

debutant.question: Did the conversion of Saul (Paul) take place before or after the stoning of Stephen?
options: At the same time as the birth of Jesus
debutant.explanation: Saul approved of Stephen's murder (Acts 8:1) before encountering the resurrected Christ on the road to Damascus (Acts 9).

debutant.question: Which prophet lived during the time of King Ahab and Jezebel?
debutant.explanation: Elijah prophesied in the Northern Kingdom during the reign of King Ahab and Queen Jezebel (1 Kings 17-21).

debutant.question: Who directly succeeded the prophet Elijah?
debutant.explanation: Elisha received a double portion of Elijah's spirit when Elijah was taken up to heaven (2 Kings 2:9-15).

debutant.question: What event precedes Daniel's entry into the lions' den?
debutant.explanation: Daniel was taken as a young man to Babylon during the deportation under Nebuchadnezzar (Daniel 1).

debutant.question: How many years did the Jewish people remain in exile in Babylon according to Jeremiah's prophecy?
debutant.explanation: Jeremiah predicted that the desolation would last 70 years before the return to Judah (Jeremiah 25:11; 29:10).

debutant.question: Who led the rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem after the exile?
debutant.explanation: Nehemiah returned from Shushan under King Artaxerxes to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem in 52 days (Nehemiah 2 and 6:15).

debutant.question: In how many days were the walls of Jerusalem rebuilt under Nehemiah?
debutant.explanation: Nehemiah 6:15 records that the wall was completed in 52 days despite opposition.

debutant.question: Which prophet preached in Nineveh long before the fall of Jerusalem?
debutant.explanation: Jonah prophesied to Nineveh in the 8th century BC. BC, while Haggai, Zechariah and Malachi are post-exilic.

debutant.question: In what order did these three women in the Bible live?
debutant.explanation: Sarah lived in the time of the patriarchs (~2000 BC), Ruth in the time of the Judges (~1100 BC), and Mary in the 1st century.

debutant.question: How many days had Lazarus already been in the tomb when Jesus resurrected him?
debutant.explanation: Martha reminded Jesus that Lazarus had been in the tomb for four days (John 11:39).

debutant.question: What event occurred during King Belshazzar's feast in Babylon?
options: The appearance of a hand writing on the wall
debutant.explanation: During Belshazzar's feast, a hand wrote on the wall, announcing the fall of Babylon that night (Daniel 5).

debutant.question: Who ruled in Jerusalem when the Roman census edict brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem?
debutant.explanation: Luke 2:1 mentions an edict from Caesar Augustus ordering a census of all the inhabited earth.

debutant.question: What event marks the end of the book of Acts of the Apostles?
options: Paul preaching in Rome for two years
debutant.explanation: Acts 28:30-31 ends with Paul staying two full years in Rome and boldly announcing the Kingdom.

debutant.question: How many times a day did Daniel pray despite King Darius' decree?
debutant.explanation: Daniel continued to kneel three times a day with the windows open toward Jerusalem (Daniel 6:10).

debutant.question: How many years old was Abraham when Isaac was born?
debutant.explanation: Genesis 21:5 indicates that Abraham was 100 years old when his son Isaac was born.

debutant.question: At what age did Abraham leave Haran at the call of God?
debutant.explanation: Abraham was 75 years old when he left Haran for the land of Canaan (Genesis 12:4).

debutant.question: How many years did Jacob work for Laban to marry Rachel and Leah?
debutant.explanation: Jacob served Laban 7 years for Rachel, received Leah by trickery, then served another 7 years for Rachel (Genesis 29:18-30).

debutant.question: Which king built the first Temple approximately 480 years after the Exodus?
debutant.explanation: 1 Kings 6:1 places the beginning of Solomon's construction of the Temple 480 years after the exodus from Egypt.

debutant.question: In what order do these kings of Judah appear: Josiah, Hezekiah, Solomon?
debutant.explanation: Solomon reigned in the 10th century. av. BC, Hezekiah in the 8th-7th century. av. BC, and Josiah at the end of the 7th century. av. AD

debutant.question: Which book of the New Testament was written last according to the majority of scholars?
options: The Apocalypse (or the Gospel of John)
debutant.explanation: The Johannine writings (Gospel of John, epistles and Revelation) are generally dated to the end of the 1st century (around 90-96 AD).

debutant.question: How many days passed between the presentation of Jesus by the shepherds and the visit of the wise men?
options: Several months or even up to two years later
debutant.explanation: The wise men found the child in a house (Matthew 2:11), and Herod killed the boys until they were two years old according to the date given.

debutant.question: Which apostle was executed by Herod Agrippa I around 44 AD? AD?
debutant.explanation: Acts 12:1-2 records that Herod put James, John's brother, to death with the sword.

debutant.question: How many years was Israel ruled by Saul according to Acts 13:21?
debutant.explanation: Paul recalls in Acts 13:21 that God gave them Saul for 40 years.

intermediaire.question: In what chronological order should these patriarchs be placed: Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob?
intermediaire.explanation: Order: Noah (after creation) → Abraham (c. 2000 BC) → Isaac (his son) → Jacob (son of Isaac).

intermediaire.question: When was the first Temple in Jerusalem destroyed?
intermediaire.explanation: Solomon's Temple was destroyed by Nebuchadnezzar in 586 BC. BC during the capture of Jerusalem.

intermediaire.question: What period approximately corresponds to Moses historically?
intermediaire.explanation: Most historians place Moses and the Exodus around 1280-1250 BC. BC under Ramses II of Egypt.

intermediaire.question: In what order do the great empires of Daniel 2 follow one another?
intermediaire.explanation: Daniel 2 and 7: Babylon (gold) → Persia (silver) → Greece (brass) → Rome (iron). Order corresponding to historical succession.

intermediaire.question: When did the prophets Amos and Hosea prophesie?
options: Period of the United Kingdom under David/Solomon
Period of the divided kingdom (8th century BC)
intermediaire.explanation: Amos and Hosea prophesied in the 8th century BC (around 760-720), in the Northern Kingdom, shortly before the fall of Samaria (722 BC).

intermediaire.question: What is the approximate date of the writing of the oldest Gospel?
intermediaire.explanation: Mark, considered the oldest gospel, is generally dated to 65-70 AD. BC, before or after the destruction of the Temple.

intermediaire.question: When did the city of Samaria (Northern Kingdom) fall?
intermediaire.explanation: Samaria fell in 722 BC. BC under Sargon II of Assyria, leading to the deportation of the 10 tribes (2 Kings 17).

intermediaire.question: When did Paul write his epistles chronologically?
intermediaire.explanation: The Epistles of Paul (c. 50-62 AD) are the oldest NT texts, predating the written Gospels.

intermediaire.question: In what chronological order should these books of the NT be placed: John, Mark, Acts, Revelation?
intermediaire.explanation: Approximate dating: Mark (65-70) → Acts (80-85) → John (90-95) → Revelation (95-96 AD).

intermediaire.question: When did Alexander the Great conquer Judea?
intermediaire.explanation: Alexander the Great conquered Palestine in 333-332 BC. BC, opening the Hellenistic period which would have a profound impact on Judaism.

intermediaire.question: Approximately how long did Abraham and Jesus last?
intermediaire.explanation: Abraham is dated around 2000 BC. BC and Jesus was born around 4-6 BC. BC, approximately 2000 years apart.

intermediaire.question: Approximately when did the destruction of the Second Temple take place?
intermediaire.explanation: The Second Temple was destroyed by Titus and the Roman armies in 70 AD. BC, as Jesus prophesied (Matthew 24:2).

intermediaire.question: What OT event immediately precedes the period of Judges?
options: The conquest of Canaan under Joshua
intermediaire.explanation: The conquest of Canaan under Joshua immediately precedes the period of the Judges. After Joshua's death, each tribe had its own rulers (Judges 1-2).

intermediaire.question: When did Jeremiah prophesy about the Babylonian exile?
options: Before and during the exile (from approximately 627 BC until 586)
intermediaire.explanation: Jeremiah began prophesying in 627 BC. (reign of Josiah) and continued through the destruction of Jerusalem in 586 BC. AD

intermediaire.question: In what order did the 3 kings of the United Kingdom reign?
intermediaire.explanation: Order of the first 3 kings: Saul (around 1050-1010) → David (around 1010-970) → Solomon (around 970-931 BC).

intermediaire.question: In what chronological order should these Old Testament prophets be placed?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah prophesied in the 8th century. av. BC, Jeremiah in the 7th-6th century. av. BC, and Haggai after the exile around 520 BC. AD

intermediaire.question: In approximately what year did Cyrus the Great issue his edict allowing the return of the Jews?
intermediaire.explanation: After the capture of Babylon in 539 BC. BC, Cyrus issued the Edict of Return in 538 BC. (Ezra 1:1).

intermediaire.question: In approximately what year was the Second Temple completed under Zerubbabel?
intermediaire.explanation: Completed the 6th year of the reign of Darius I, in 516/515 BC. BC, or 70 years after the destruction of 586 BC. (Ezra 6:15).

intermediaire.question: Which Assyrian king besieged Jerusalem during the reign of Hezekiah in 701 BC? AD?
intermediaire.explanation: Sennacherib besieged Jerusalem in 701 BC. AD, but the city was miraculously delivered (2 Kings 18-19).

intermediaire.question: In what year did the first deportation of Judah to Babylon (with Daniel) take place?
intermediaire.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar subdued Judah and took elite captives, including Daniel, in 605 BC. (Daniel 1:1).

intermediaire.question: In what year were King Jehoiachin and the prophet Ezekiel deported to Babylon?
intermediaire.explanation: The second deportation took place in 597 BC. BC, including King Jehoiachin and Ezekiel (2 Kings 24:10-16).

intermediaire.question: Under which king of Judah was the Book of the Law found in the Temple around 622 BC? AD?
intermediaire.explanation: In the 18th year of Josiah's reign (~622 BC), the high priest Hilkiah found the Book of the Law (2 Kings 22).

intermediaire.question: How long did King Josiah reign over Judah?
intermediaire.explanation: Josiah became king at age 8 and reigned for 31 years in Jerusalem (2 Kings 22:1).

intermediaire.question: In approximately what year did the Battle of Carchemish take place between Babylon and Egypt?
intermediaire.explanation: In 605 BC. In 500 BC, Nebuchadnezzar defeated Pharaoh Neco at Carchemish, bringing the Middle East under Babylonian domination (Jeremiah 46:2).

intermediaire.question: In what order did these post-exilic prophets follow one another?
intermediaire.explanation: Haggai and Zechariah prophesied around 520-518 BC. AD for the reconstruction of the Temple; Malachi prophesied in the 5th century. av. AD

intermediaire.question: Under which Persian emperor did Nehemiah return to Jerusalem around 445 BC? AD?
intermediaire.explanation: Nehemiah obtained permission from Artaxerxes I in the 20th year of his reign (~445 BC, Nehemiah 2:1).

intermediaire.question: Approximately in what year did Ezra return to Jerusalem?
intermediaire.explanation: Ezra left in the 7th year of Artaxerxes I, traditionally dated 458 BC. (Ezra 7:7-8).

intermediaire.question: What event marked the end of the intertestamental period on the Roman side?
options: The capture of Jerusalem by Pompey (63 BC)
The destruction of the Temple (70 AD)
intermediaire.explanation: In 63 BC. BC, the Roman general Pompey took Jerusalem and placed Judea under Roman rule.

intermediaire.question: In what year did the Maccabean revolt against Antiochus IV Epiphanes begin?
intermediaire.explanation: In 167 BC. BC, Antiochus IV desecrated the Temple, triggering the Maccabean revolt (Hanukkah festival in 164 BC).

intermediaire.question: What is the approximate date of the birth of Jesus today?
intermediaire.explanation: Herod the Great having died in 4 BC. BC, the birth of Jesus is between 6 and 4 BC. AD

intermediaire.question: What year is most commonly used for the crucifixion of Jesus?
intermediaire.explanation: Under Pontius Pilate (prefect from 26 to 36 AD), the dates 30 or 33 AD. AD correspond to possible Fridays 14 Nisan.

intermediaire.question: In what approximate year did the Council of Jerusalem take place (Acts 15)?
intermediaire.explanation: The Apostolic Council of Jerusalem was held around 48-49 AD. AD to rule on the reception of pagans.

intermediaire.question: In what year did Emperor Claudius expel the Jews from Rome (Acts 18:2)?
intermediaire.explanation: The edict of Claudius around 49 AD. BC chased Aquila and Priscilla from Rome to Corinth, where Paul met them.

intermediaire.question: Which Roman governor in Corinth provides a key chronological marker for Paul's stay (AD 51-52)?
intermediaire.explanation: The Delphi inscription places Gallio's proconsulate in Corinth in AD 51-52. (Acts 18:12).

intermediaire.question: Under which Roman emperor did Paul and Peter likely suffer martyrdom in Rome?
intermediaire.explanation: Tradition places the martyrdom of Peter and Paul in Rome under Nero between 64 and 67 AD. AD

intermediaire.question: In what year did the great fire of Rome followed by the persecution of Nero take place?
intermediaire.explanation: The burning of Rome took place in July 64 AD. AD, and Nero accused the Christians (Tacitus, Annals XV).

intermediaire.question: How many of Paul's major missionary journeys are described before his arrest?
intermediaire.explanation: Acts describes three major missionary journeys (Acts 13-14, 15-18, 18-21) before his transfer to Rome.

intermediaire.question: In what order did Paul visit these cities on his 2nd trip?
intermediaire.explanation: During the 2nd journey (Acts 16-18), Paul passed through Philippi, Thessalonica, Berea, Athens and then Corinth.

intermediaire.question: How long did Paul stay in Ephesus on his third journey?
intermediaire.explanation: In Acts 20:31, Paul reminds the elders of Ephesus that he warned them night and day for three years.

intermediaire.question: Under which king of Judah did the prophet Isaiah receive his inaugural vision (Isaiah 6:1)?
intermediaire.explanation: Isaiah 6:1 places his calling in 'the year that King Uzziah died', around 740 BC. AD

intermediaire.question: How many years did the Northern Kingdom (Israel) last between the schism (931) and the fall of Samaria (722)?
intermediaire.explanation: From 931 BC. BC to 722 BC BC, the Northern Kingdom lasted a little over two centuries (209 years).

intermediaire.question: How many years longer than Samaria did Jerusalem hold before its destruction in 586 BC? AD?
intermediaire.explanation: Between the fall of Samaria (722 BC) and that of Jerusalem (586 BC), 136 years passed.

intermediaire.question: Which king of Judah was healed and given 15 more years of life?
intermediaire.explanation: God granted King Hezekiah 15 more years after his prayer (2 Kings 20:6).

intermediaire.question: In what order did these two famous kings of Judah reign?
intermediaire.explanation: Hezekiah reigned around 715-686 BC. BC, then his son Manasseh, his grandson Amon, and his great-grandson Josiah (640-609 BC).

intermediaire.question: Which Persian king reigned at the time of the story of Esther?
intermediaire.explanation: The book of Esther takes place under Ahasuerus, identified with Xerxes I (486-465 BC).

intermediaire.question: In what order are these three post-exilic historical books located?
options: Esther (reign of Xerxes) between the return of Zerubbabel and the mission of Nehemiah
intermediaire.explanation: Zerubbabel returned around 538 BC. BC, Esther lived under Xerxes (486-465), then Ezra (458) and Nehemiah (445) under Artaxerxes I.

intermediaire.question: In what approximate year are the Gospels of Matthew and Luke often dated?
intermediaire.explanation: Many exegetes date Matthew and Luke to the years 80-85 AD. BC, after Mark (~65-70).

intermediaire.question: Which emperor reigned during John's exile on Patmos according to the dominant tradition?
intermediaire.explanation: Irenaeus of Lyon places the writing of the Apocalypse at the end of the reign of Domitian, around 95-96 AD. AD

intermediaire.question: How many days was Paul blind in Damascus before Ananias prayed for him?
intermediaire.explanation: Acts 9:9 records that Saul remained three days without seeing, eating or drinking.

intermediaire.question: How many years did Paul spend in Arabia and Damascus before going up to Peter in Jerusalem (Galatians 1:18)?
intermediaire.explanation: Paul states in Galatians 1:18 that after three years he went up to Jerusalem to meet Cephas.

intermediaire.question: How many years was Paul held in Caesarea under Felix before appearing before Festus?
intermediaire.explanation: Acts 24:27 indicates that after two years Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus.

intermediaire.question: When did the prophet Obadiah probably prophesy against Edom?
options: After a fall/looting of Jerusalem (probably 586 BC)
intermediaire.explanation: Obadiah 11-14 condemns Edom for rejoicing in the day of distress and the plundering of Jerusalem.

intermediaire.question: What historical event marked the end of the Jewish revolt of Bar Kokhba?
intermediaire.explanation: The second Jewish revolt (132-135 AD) ended in 135 AD. BC under Emperor Hadrian.

intermediaire.question: Under which pharaoh of Egypt did King Josiah die at Megiddo in 609 BC? AD?
intermediaire.explanation: Josiah opposed Pharaoh Neco II who went up to help Assyria and was killed at Megiddo in 609 BC. (2 Kings 23:29).

intermediaire.question: Which pharaoh plundered Jerusalem under Rehoboam, 5 years after the death of Solomon (~925 BC)?
intermediaire.explanation: 1 Kings 14:25-26 mentions Shishak's invasion in the 5th year of Rehoboam's reign (~925 BC).

intermediaire.question: In what order did these three judges appear in the book of Judges?
intermediaire.explanation: Deborah comes in chapters 4-5, Gideon in chapters 6-8, and Samson in chapters 13-16.

intermediaire.question: How long did the Ark of the Covenant stay in Kirjath-jearim before David transferred it?
intermediaire.explanation: 1 Samuel 7:2 records that the Ark remained for a long time in Kirjath-jearim, twenty years having elapsed before the revival under Samuel.

intermediaire.question: Approximately when did the Greek translation of the Septuagint (LXX) begin in Alexandria?
intermediaire.explanation: The translation of the Pentateuch into Greek began in Alexandria in the 3rd century BC. BC under Ptolemy II Philadelphus.

intermediaire.question: Which prophet was contemporary with the fall of Nineveh (612 BC) that he had announced?
intermediaire.explanation: Nahum announced the imminent fall of Nineveh, which actually fell in 612 BC. BC before the Babylonians and the Medes.

intermediaire.question: How long did Jesus stay in the desert after his baptism before returning to Galilee?
intermediaire.explanation: The Synoptics indicate that the Spirit led Jesus into the desert for 40 days (Mark 1:12-13).

intermediaire.question: Which ecumenical council was held in 325 AD? AD to deal with the divinity of Christ?
intermediaire.explanation: The First Council of Nicaea was convened in 325 AD. AD facing Arianism.

intermediaire.question: In what order were these epistles of Paul probably written?
intermediaire.explanation: 1 Thessalonians (~50-51) is one of the earliest, Romans dates from around 57, and 2 Timothy is the last pastoral epistle (~66-67).

expert.question: What is the generally accepted date for the division of the Kingdom of Israel?
expert.explanation: The division of the kingdom under Rehoboam is conventionally dated to 931 BC. BC, after the death of Solomon.

expert.question: What is the main challenge of the 'Judges timeline' in biblical studies?
options: The sum of the years of the Judges totals over 400 years while 1 Kings 6:1 speaks of 480 years between the Exodus and the Temple
expert.explanation: Classic problem: the cumulative sum of the periods of the Judges exceeds 400 years. The solution: some periods overlap and are regional, not national.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the number '40' in biblical chronology (40 years of desert, 40 days of flood, etc.)?
options: A symbolic Hebrew number denoting a period of complete testing/transformation, without excluding historical reality
A purely ritual number without history
expert.explanation: The Hebrew '40' is both potentially literal AND loaded with symbolic meaning (full proof). We must not oppose symbolism and history.

expert.question: What is the high vs. low dating of the Exodus and what are the implications?
options: High dating: ~1446 BC. (1 Kings 6:1); low: ~1270 BC (Ramses II). The issue: the identity of the Pharaoh of the Exodus and the archaeological correspondence
The Exodus is universally dated to 1300 BC. AD
The debate is purely theological without historical basis
expert.explanation: 1 Kings 6:1: 480 years before the Temple (970 BC) = ~1446 BC (Thoutmosis III?). The low dating (~1270) follows Ramses II and the city of Pi-Ramses.

expert.question: What is the chronological framework of documentary theory (JEDP) concerning the writing of the Pentateuch?
options: Entirely in the time of Moses (around 1300 BC)
Sources J (900 BC), E (800), D (622), P (500-400) — Pentateuch finalized around 400 BC AD
Written in the 2nd century BC. AD
expert.explanation: Documentary theory classifies: Yahwist (J, ~900), Elohist (E, ~800), Deuteronomist (D, ~622), Priestly (P, ~500-450). Strongly contested by evangelicals.

expert.question: When and how was the NT canon officially established?
options: Progressively from the 2nd to the 4th century, with the canon of Athanasius (367 AD) and the councils of Carthage (397, 419)
By a formal apostolic decision of the 1st century
expert.explanation: The process of canonization of the NT: increasing use since the 2nd century, list of Athanasius (367), Council of Carthage (397) confirming the 27 books.

expert.question: How did the writing of the Gospel of John date in relation to the Johannine epistles and the Apocalypse?
options: Gospel (~90-95) → Epistles (95-100) → Apocalypse (95-96 or earlier under Nero)
Apocalypse written before the Gospel according to Neronian dating
Both dates are also attested in the manuscripts
expert.explanation: Dominant dating: Gospel of John (~90-95), Epistles John (~90-100), Apocalypse (~95-96 under Domitian, or ~65-68 under Nero according to Neronian dating).

expert.question: What is the chronological relationship between the epistles of Paul and the writing of the synoptic gospels?
options: The epistles of Paul (50-62) precede the synoptic gospels (Mark ~65-70; Matthew and Luke ~80-85)
expert.explanation: The Pauline epistles (50-62 AD) constitute the oldest written Christian texts we have, predating the written gospels.

expert.question: What is the challenge of OT 'absolute chronology' versus internal biblical chronology?
options: No challenge: the two match perfectly
The sum of the years of the kings of Israel and Judah does not correspond exactly to the Assyrian and Babylonian chronologies, requiring corrections for coregencies
expert.explanation: Thiele's royal lists (1951): numerous coregencies and different counting systems explain the apparent discrepancies. Synchronization with Assyria and Babylon is possible within ±1-2 years.

expert.question: What is the theological significance of the concept of 'fullness of times' (Galatians 4:4) in biblical chronology?
options: The conviction that the incarnation arrives at the precise moment desired by God: pax romana, Greek koiné, Jewish diaspora, intensified messianic expectation
A purely eschatological concept of the future
expert.explanation: The 'pleroma tou chronou' (Galatians 4:4): the Pax Romana (safe roads), the common Greek language, the global Jewish diaspora and intensified messianic expectation created a unique providential context.

expert.question: What is the difference between the 'chronos' and 'kairos' calendar in biblical theology of time?
options: 'Chronos' = sequential quantitative time; 'Kairos' = opportune moment charged with theological and decisive meaning — God's time in history
expert.explanation: 'Chronos' (χρόνος) = succession of measurable time. 'Kairos' (καιρός) = decisive, timely and theologically charged moment. The Incarnation is the Kairos par excellence (Mark 1:15).

expert.question: What is the meaning of 'millennium' in Revelation 20 and the 3 major interpretations?
options: A literal future reign of 1000 years: only interpretation
(1) Premillennialism: future literal reign; (2) Amillennialism: symbolic period (Church era); (3) Postmillennialism: gradual reign before the return of Christ
expert.explanation: The 3 positions: (1) Premillennialism — Christ returns BEFORE the literal millennium; (2) Amillennialism — the millennium = present reign of Christ (patristic majority); (3) Postmillennialism — the millennium precedes the return of Christ.

expert.question: What is the dating of the book of Daniel and the debate between prophetic interpretation and Maccabean writing?
options: Lives. (internal date of the author Daniel) vs. 2nd c. (165 BC, critical position: 'prophecies after the fact' of the Maccabean era)
expert.explanation: Daniel appears as written in the 6th century. (Babylonian exile). Historical criticism dates its writing to ~165 BC. (Antiochus IV) — 'vaticinium ex eventu'. Issue: the possibility of predictive prophecy.

expert.question: What is the chronological relationship between the Jewish Passover and the death of Jesus according to the synopsis of the gospels?
options: The synoptics place the Last Supper on the evening of Passover; John places it on the day before (14 Nisan) — classic tension in exegesis
John and the synoptics are identical
The date is impossible to determine
expert.explanation: Classic tension: synoptics (the Last Supper = paschal meal, 15 Nisan) vs John (Jesus dies on 14 Nisan, when the paschal lamb was being immolated). Several solutions proposed.

expert.question: What is the chronological framework of the Protestant Reformation and its relationship with the rediscovery of the Bible?
expert.explanation: The Protestant Reformation: Luther published his 95 theses in 1517. The invention of printing (Gutenberg ~1450) and the rediscovery of NT Greek (Erasmus 1516) made possible the diffusion of the Bible in vernacular languages.

expert.question: Which Egyptian stele dated to around 1208 BC? BC contains the oldest known extrabiblical mention of the name 'Israel'?
expert.explanation: The Merenptah stele (around 1208 BC) mentions 'Israel is devastated, its seed is no more', confirming its presence in Canaan in the 13th century. av. AD

expert.question: What battle of 853 BC? BC, mentioned on the Kurkh monolith, cites King Ahab of Israel?
expert.explanation: The Assyrian monolith of Shalmanesar III cites 'Ahab the Israelite' with 2000 chariots at the Battle of Qarqar in 853 BC. AD

expert.question: On which Assyrian obelisk do we see King Jehu of Israel prostrating himself before Shalmanesar III around 841 BC? AD?
expert.explanation: The Black Obelisk of Nimrud depicts 'Jehu, son of Omri' paying tribute to Shalmanesar III in 841 BC. AD

expert.question: Which Aramaic inscription from the 9th century BC? AD mentions the 'House of David' (Bytdwd)?
expert.explanation: Discovered in 1993-1994, the Tel Dan stele (~840 BC) mentions the victory over a king of the 'House of David'.

expert.question: In what precise year do the Babylonian tablets date the capture of Jerusalem during the 2nd deportation (Jehoiachin)?
expert.explanation: The Babylonian Chronicle (BM 21946) fixes the capitulation of Jerusalem on 2 Adar of the 7th year of Nebuchadnezzar, i.e. March 16, 597 BC. AD

expert.question: How does Edwin Thiele (The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings) explain the apparent discrepancies in the chronology of the kings of Israel and Judah?
options: By coregencies, years of accession vs non-accession, and calendars starting in Nisan or Tishri
By the late invention of the monarchy
expert.explanation: Thiele showed that Judah and Israel used different systems (Nisan vs. Tishri, year of accession vs. non-accession) as well as coregencies.

expert.question: What chronological difference separates the beginning of the royal year in Judah (Tishri) and in Northern Israel (Nisan)?
expert.explanation: Israel counted the years of reign from Nisan (spring), while Judah used Tishri (fall), a gap of 6 months.

expert.question: According to 2 Kings 25:8, in what month of the Hebrew calendar was Solomon's Temple burned in 586 BC? AD?
expert.explanation: The Temple was burned in the 5th month (Ab), still commemorated today by the fast of Tisha B'Av.

expert.question: Which Persian document from 539 BC. AD confirms Cyrus' policy of sending people and cults back to their sanctuaries?
expert.explanation: The Cylinder of Cyrus attests to the imperial policy of religious tolerance and restoration of local sanctuaries after the fall of Babylon.

expert.question: When do the Aramaic Elephantine papyri mention the sons of Sanballat, governor of Samaria (contemporary of Nehemiah)?
expert.explanation: Elephantine's letters dated 407 BC AD mention Delaiah and Shélémya, sons of Sanballat, confirming the dating of Nehemiah in the 5th century BC. AD

expert.question: What date marks the entry of Antiochus IV Epiphanes and the desecration of the Temple by the 'abomination of desolation' (1 Maccabees 1:54)?
expert.explanation: 15/25 Kislev 167 BC BC, a pagan altar was erected on the altar of burnt offerings; the Temple was reconsecrated exactly 3 years later (164 BC).

expert.question: What is the usually debated starting point for the '70 weeks of years' (490 years) of Daniel 9:25?
options: The edict of Cyrus (538), the edict of Artaxerxes for Ezra (458/457) or for Nehemiah (445/444)
The death of Alexander the Great (323)
expert.explanation: Messianic interpretations calculate the 69 weeks (483 years) from the decrees of Artaxerxes (457 or 444 BC) until the ministry or death of Jesus.

expert.question: Which inscription discovered at Caesarea Maritime in 1961 confirms the historicity and exact title of Pontius Pilate?
expert.explanation: The Pilate Stone mentions 'Pontius Pilatus, Praefectus Iudaeae', confirming its exact title under Tiberius (AD 26-36).

expert.question: In what specific year is the 15th year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar (Luke 3:1), marking the beginning of the ministry of John the Baptist, located?
expert.explanation: Tiberius succeeded Augustus in AD 14. AD (or was associated in 12): his 15th year therefore corresponds to 27-29 AD. AD

expert.question: Why does the mention of '46 years' to build the Temple in John 2:20 help date the beginning of Jesus' ministry?
options: Herod began the work in 20/19 BC. AD, which places this Passover around 27-28 AD. AD
The Temple was destroyed 46 years later
It is a purely symbolic figure with no historical link.
expert.explanation: According to Flavius ​​Josephus, Herod undertook the renovation of the Temple in 20/19 BC. AD; 46 years later leads to exactly 27-28 AD. AD

expert.question: Which Pauline chronology is based on the edict of Claudius (49) and the proconsulate of Gallio (51-52)?
options: The dating of the writing of the Apocalypse
Paul's 18-month stay in Corinth during the 2nd journey (AD 50-52)
The birth of Paul in Tarsus
expert.explanation: The recent arrival of Aquila and Priscilla (edit of 49) and the appearance before Gallio (51-52) firmly anchor the Pauline chronology.

expert.question: How does the account of the visit to Jerusalem in Galatians 2:1-10 differ from that in Acts?
options: No difference, everything is the same
Scholars debate whether it corresponds to the famine visitation (Acts 11:30, ~46) or to the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15, ~49)
Galatians 2 talks about the trip to Rome
expert.explanation: The identification of Galatians 2 with Acts 11 (early dating of Galatians, ~48) or Acts 15 (~50-55) is a classic debate in New Testament chronology.

expert.question: What is the chronological range used for the writing of the Dead Sea Scrolls (Qumran)?
options: 8th century. av. BC to 6th century. av. AD
3rd century av. BC to 1st century after (before AD 68)
2nd century after BC to 4th century after AD
expert.explanation: The Qumran Scrolls cover approximately 250 BC. BC to AD 68 BC, date of the destruction of the site by the Roman legions.

expert.question: Which papyrus from the 2nd century AD? is generally recognized as the oldest preserved fragment of the New Testament?
options: The Rylands Papyrus P52 (John 18, c. 125 AD)
expert.explanation: P52 (fragment of John 18:31-33, 37-38) is paleographically dated around 125 AD. AD, a few decades after the writing of John.

expert.question: In what approximate year is the Muratori fragment (oldest known Latin canonical list in the NT) usually dated?
expert.explanation: The Muratori Canon, generally dated to the end of the 2nd century (~170-200), already testifies to a very broad canonical core of the NT.

expert.question: In the chronology of the Letters of the Apostle Paul, which group is generally referred to as the 'captivity epistles'?
expert.explanation: Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians and Philemon were written during Paul's imprisonment (traditionally in Rome around AD 60-62).

expert.question: Which Roman emperor besieged Jerusalem in AD 70? AD as a general before becoming emperor in 79?
expert.explanation: Titus, son of Emperor Vespasian, completed the siege and took Jerusalem in August–September 70 AD. AD

expert.question: Which first-century Jewish historian provides the primary extrabiblical source on the Second Temple period and the war of 66-70?
expert.explanation: Flavius ​​Josephus (Jewish War, Jewish Antiquities) is a major historical source for 1st century Judaism.

expert.question: Approximately how long separates the return of Nehemiah (445 BC) from the birth of Jesus (~5 BC)?
options: 440 years (often called the '400 years of silence')
expert.explanation: Between Malachi/Nehemiah (5th century BC) and John the Baptist extends the intertestamental period of approximately four centuries.

expert.question: What chronological difference exists between the Masoretic Text (TM) and the Septuagint (LXX) in the genealogies of Genesis 5 and 11?
options: The LXX adds approximately 1400 to 1500 years to the chronology of the patriarchs before Abraham
expert.explanation: In the LXX, several patriarchs father their sons 100 years later than in the TM, extending the antediluvian and postdiluvian chronology.

expert.question: Which 17th century scholar calculated the creation of the world in 4004 BC? BC from biblical genealogies?
expert.explanation: Archbishop James Ussher published his Annales Veteris Testamenti (1650), setting the creation at October 23, 4004 BC. AD

expert.question: Which 6th century monk established the 'Anno Domini' dating system (AD) by calculating the birth of Christ?
expert.explanation: Dionysius the Small (around 525) established the Christian era, with a slight delay of a few years compared to the death of Herod (4 BC).

expert.question: What is the time of the prophet Elisha according to the chronology of the kings of Israel?
options: Mid-to-late 9th century BC BC (from Joram to Joash)
expert.explanation: Elisha ministered from about 850 to 800 BC. BC, under Joram, Jehu, Jehoahaz and Joash of Israel.

expert.question: What date corresponds to the fall of the Neo-Babylonian kingdom to Cyrus the Great?
expert.explanation: Babylon fell to Cyrus' Medo-Persian troops in October 539 BC. (Daniel 5:30).

expert.question: In what approximate year did Nebuchadnezzar II die, giving way to Amel-Marduk (Evil-Merodach) who freed Jehoiachin (2 Kings 25:27)?
expert.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar died in 562 BC. AD; his son Amel-Marduk pardoned King Jehoiachin in the 37th year of his captivity.

expert.question: What time period does Joel's prophecy take place according to the two main exegetical hypotheses?
options: Only in the 10th century BC. AD
Either pre-exilic (9th century under Joash) or post-exilic (5th-4th century BC)
expert.explanation: The absence of mention of the king and the central place of the Temple and the priests divide researchers between the 9th century. and the 5th-4th century. av. AD

expert.question: What is the chronological framework of the 'Letters of Lachish' discovered in 1935?
options: The last days before the fall of Jerusalem to Babylon (588-586 BC)
The era of the Maccabees (165 BC)
The Roman siege of 70 AD AD
expert.explanation: These ancient Hebrew ostraca date from Nebuchadnezzar's final campaign against Judah around 588-586 BC. AD

expert.question: In approximately what year was the Edict of Milan (tolerance towards Christianity) promulgated by Constantine and Licinius?
expert.explanation: The Edict of Milan in 313 AD. BC ended imperial persecutions and granted freedom of worship to Christians.

expert.question: Which emperor made Nicene Christianity the official religion of the Roman Empire by the Edict of Thessalonica (380)?
expert.explanation: Theodosius I promulgated the Edict of Thessalonica in 380 AD. BC, making Christianity the state religion.

expert.question: In what year did Saint Jerome complete most of the Latin translation of the Vulgate?
expert.explanation: Jerome worked in Bethlehem from 382 to approximately 405 AD. AD to translate the Bible into Latin from Hebrew and Greek.

expert.question: In the chronology of Luke's Gospel, when does the 'great ascent to Jerusalem' (Luke 9:51 - 19:27) begin?
options: After the Transfiguration and the sending of the disciples, a major turning point in the ministry
expert.explanation: Luke 9:51 ('he resolutely took the road to Jerusalem') structures the entire second half of his gospel towards the Passion.

expert.question: How many distinct Easters are explicitly mentioned in the Gospel of John, allowing us to estimate the duration of Jesus' ministry?
options: At least 3 Easters (John 2:13; 6:4; 11:55), suggesting approximately 3 years of ministry
expert.explanation: While the Synoptics only mention one final Passover, John names at least three, basing the estimate of a ministry of ~3 years.

expert.question: What a political event of 44 AD? BC described in Acts 12 is also dated by Flavius ​​Josephus?
options: The sudden death of Herod Agrippa I in Caesarea
expert.explanation: Acts 12:20-23 and Flavius ​​Josephus (Antiquities 19.8.2) both describe the sudden death of Herod Agrippa I in AD 44. AD

expert.question: What is the name of the proconsul of Cyprus converted by Paul around 46-47 AD? (Acts 13:7)?
expert.explanation: Sergius Paulus is epigraphically attested as proconsul of Cyprus in the mid-1st century AD. AD

expert.question: What dating separates the Council of Nicaea (325) from the Council of Chalcedon (451) in the formation of classical Christology?
expert.explanation: Between Nicaea (325, divinity of the Son) and Chalcedon (451, two natures in one person), 126 years of Christological debates passed.

expert.question: In what approximate year were the Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus copied?
expert.explanation: These two large complete or almost complete Greek uncials of the Bible date from the middle of the 4th century AD. AD

expert.question: What a historical crisis of 735-732 BC. J.-C. provoked the oracle of Emmanuel in Isaiah 7?
options: The Syro-Ephraimite War (coalition of Aram and Israel against Ahaz of Judah)
The invasion of Alexander the Great
expert.explanation: Rezîn of Damascus and Peqah of Israel besieged Jerusalem in 735-732 BC. to force Ahaz to join their anti-Assyrian coalition.

expert.question: How long did the Temple in Jerusalem lie in ruins between 586 BC and 586 BC? AD and the dedication of the Second Temple in 516 BC. AD?
expert.explanation: From 586 BC BC to 516 BC B.C., exactly 70 years passed, fulfilling from another angle the 70 years of Jeremiah.

expert.question: What period of biblical history corresponds to the Middle Bronze Age (~2000-1550 BC)?
options: The time of the Patriarchs (Abraham, Isaac, Jacob)
expert.explanation: The legal and pastoral customs of the patriarchal stories reflect the context of the Middle Bronze Age (~2000-1700 BC).

expert.question: In what chronological order were these three synoptics or writings written according to the two-source hypothesis?
options: Mark + Source Q → Matthew and Luke
expert.explanation: The prevailing hypothesis assumes that Matthew and Luke used the Gospel of Mark (~65-70) as well as a common source of sayings (Q).

expert.question: What date marks the schism between the Western Church and the Eastern Church in the history of Christianity?
expert.explanation: The Great Schism of 1054 separated Rome and Constantinople, well after the biblical period but heir to ancient debates.
